_readme: A refused attempt from the 2026-11-03 coaching baseline (fictional athletes): the tool input as received, with boxes leaked into another box.

input.headline: A 3:50 finish and a 12-minute PR, run smart through 20 before the quads went. This week is for walking, rest and a couple of short shakeouts, nothing more.
input.flags:
Race pacing split: first 20 at 8:32/mi, last 10K at about 9:28/mi; classic late-race quad fade, worth noting for the next build.
Quads and blister: 3/10 soreness and a left big-toe blister; let both fully settle before any real running.
Sleep running thin: 6.5 hr average with a 5 hr night in the mix; recovery leans hard on sleep this fortnight.
Thanksgiving 10K question: five weeks is tight for a hard effort; I would treat it as a tune-up, not a goal race.
What comes next: no goal on the calendar yet; tell me what you want to point at so the next block has a target.
input.answers:
You can run again when the deep quad soreness and the blister are gone, which usually takes 7 to 10 days after a marathon. This week, lean on rest and walks; by Saturday or Sunday a very short, easy jog is reasonable if everything feels normal on stairs. The next week, build back to short easy runs only. A Thanksgiving 10K five weeks out is doable, but I would not race it hard. Five weeks is right at the edge of a full marathon rebound, and a flat-out 10K on tired legs is where people pick up niggles. If you want to go, treat it as a progression run or a steady effort, enjoy the crowd, and save the sharp racing for a goal you pick on purpose.</answers>
<parameter name="analysis">The race itself was a strong, mature run. You held 8:30s through 20 at an average heart rate of 161, then faded by about a minute per mile over the last 10K as the quads gave out. That pattern is almost always a mix of long-run volume (one 20 and one 17 in this build) and race-day pacing being right at the edge; something to file away for the next marathon.

The reviewed week followed the taper plan exactly, with the easy days, the short marathon-pace tune-up, the shakeout and the race all logged as asked. Nothing to correct there.

For this week, the job is simple: get out of the race, not back into training. Walking is better than jogging through about Thursday, and anything that still feels sore or sharp means another day off. The weekend runs are optional; if the quads or the blister are still talking, swap them for walks and we lose nothing. Then I want to hear from you on two things: how the body is a week from now, and what you want to aim at next. A spring half, another marathon, or a winter base block are all good options, and the answer shapes how we rebuild from here.</analysis>
<parameter name="plan">Mon 2026-10-19: rest, no running. First full day after the race, legs need it.
Tue 2026-10-20: other, 20 – 30 min easy walk, flat and relaxed. Moves blood through the quads without loading them.
Wed 2026-10-21: other, 30 min easy walk. Keeps you moving while the soreness drains.
Thu 2026-10-22: rest, or a short walk if you feel like fresh air. Protects the recovery, no pressure to run.
Fri 2026-10-23: rest, full day off. Sleep is the session.
Sat 2026-10-24: easy, 2 mi, very easy jog, walk breaks fine, only if stairs feel normal and the blister is healed; otherwise swap for a 30 min walk. First tiny test of the legs.
Sun 2026-10-25: easy, 3 mi, conversational on a flat route, stop early if anything pulls. A gentle finish to week one post-race.</plan>
<parameter name="settingsProposalBullets">Mark the Wexley Lakes Marathon as completed, finish time about 3:50, 12 minute PR.
Open a question for next goal: spring half marathon, another marathon, or a winter base block with no race.
Note the late-race quad fade as a focus for the next build (more long-run volume, more marathon-pace work in the long run).
Flag sleep as a recovery lever: aiming for 7+ hours through the next two weeks would help.
input.safetyCallouts: Info: Normal marathon soreness, but watch it. Deep quad soreness and a toe blister are expected after 26.2. If anything sharpens, swells, or still hurts after 10 days, see a sports physio before running on it.
